title: Transpose a Matrix

concept.title: Rows become columns
body: A matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns is read with two indexes: `g[i][j]` is the value in row `i` and column `j`. The **transpose** swaps the roles of the two indexes: the value `g[i][j]` goes to row `j`, column `i`. The result has `m` rows and `n` columns.
Printing the new row `j` means walking down the old column `j`.

statement: Print the transpose of a matrix with `n` rows and `m` columns.
inputFormat: The next `n` lines have `m` integers each.

examples.note: The first column 1 4 becomes the first row.

hints: The result has m rows and n columns.
Row j of the result is column j of the input.
Use two loops: j on the outside, i on the inside, and print `g[i][j]`.

starter.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

# Your code here

explanation: Print row `j` of the result by reading the old matrix down column `j`.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * m), space O(1) besides the output.

code.python:
n, m = map(int, input().split())
g = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(n)]

for j in range(m):
    print(*[g[i][j] for i in range(n)])
